questions.stem: According to Genesis 1, on which day did God create the sun, the moon and the stars?
questions.explanation: Light was made on the first day, but the greater and lesser lights and the stars were made on the fourth day (Genesis 1:14-19).

questions.stem: According to Genesis 2, the LORD God formed man from
options: the clay of the river bank
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:7 says God formed man of dust from the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.

questions.stem: In Genesis 1, God gave human beings dominion over the fish, the birds and every living thing. This shows that human beings are
options: owners who may destroy creation freely
questions.explanation: Dominion is a trust from God; mankind manages creation on his behalf (Genesis 1:28).

questions.stem: According to Genesis 2, the LORD God put the man in the garden of Eden
options: to till it and keep it
to guard the tree of life with a sword
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:15 shows that work was part of God's purpose for man from the beginning.

questions.stem: God created the woman in Genesis 2 because
options: the animals asked for a companion
it was not good that the man should be alone
the man needed someone to name the animals
questions.explanation: God said it was not good for the man to be alone and made a helper fit for him (Genesis 2:18).

questions.stem: The statement in Genesis 1 that man was created 'in the image of God' implies that
options: God has a physical body like man
every human being has dignity and a special relationship with God
man and animals are equal in every way
questions.explanation: Being made in God's image gives every person worth and the capacity to relate to God, regardless of status.

questions.topic: God, the Controller of the universe
questions.stem: How long did it rain on the earth during the flood in the time of Noah?
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:12 says rain fell upon the earth forty days and forty nights.

questions.topic: God, the Controller of the universe
questions.stem: After the flood, the sign of God's covenant never again to destroy all flesh by a flood was
questions.explanation: God set his bow in the cloud as a sign of the covenant (Genesis 9:13).

questions.topic: God, the Controller of the universe
questions.stem: God's control of the universe was shown during the Exodus when
options: Pharaoh's daughter found Moses in a basket
the waters of the Red Sea were divided for the Israelites to cross on dry ground
Jethro advised Moses to appoint judges
questions.explanation: God drove the sea back with a strong east wind, showing his power over nature (Exodus 14:21-22).

questions.topic: God, the Controller of the universe
questions.stem: The main lesson of the flood story about God as controller of the universe is that
options: God judges wickedness but preserves those who are righteous
God is unable to control water
God destroys the world every generation
questions.explanation: God punished the corrupt world but saved Noah, a righteous man, and his household.

questions.stem: Joseph's brothers sold him to traders for
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:28 says they sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty shekels of silver.

questions.stem: In Egypt, Joseph interpreted the dreams of two officials of Pharaoh in prison. They were
options: the captain of the guard and his wife
the priest of On and his son
the chief butler and the chief baker
the chief cook and the chief soldier
questions.explanation: Genesis 40 records the dreams of Pharaoh's butler (cupbearer) and baker.

questions.stem: Pharaoh's dream of seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean cows was interpreted by Joseph to mean
options: seven years of war followed by peace
seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine
questions.explanation: Joseph explained that the dreams foretold plenty and then famine (Genesis 41).

questions.stem: Which leadership quality did Joseph show when he advised Pharaoh to store a fifth of the produce in the years of plenty?
questions.explanation: Joseph planned ahead to save Egypt and the nations from famine.

questions.stem: When his brothers feared revenge after Jacob's death, Joseph told them, 'You meant evil against me; but God meant it for good.' This shows that Joseph
options: saw God's purpose in his suffering and forgave his brothers
wanted them to become his slaves
questions.explanation: Genesis 50:20 shows Joseph's forgiveness and his trust in God's providence.

questions.stem: God called Moses from a burning bush while he was keeping the flock of
questions.explanation: Exodus 3:1 says Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro, the priest of Midian.

questions.stem: When Moses asked God's name at the burning bush, God replied,
options: 'I am the God of the Egyptians'
'I am the Holy One of Israel'
questions.explanation: Exodus 3:14 gives the divine name 'I AM WHO I AM'.

questions.stem: Moses objected to God's call because he said he was slow of speech. God responded by
options: appointing Aaron to speak for him
questions.explanation: God appointed Aaron, Moses' brother, as his spokesman (Exodus 4:14-16).

questions.stem: Jethro advised Moses to appoint able men as rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens because
options: Moses was wearing himself out by judging all the people alone
the people refused to listen to Moses
Moses wanted to return to Egypt
questions.explanation: Exodus 18 shows the value of delegation in leadership.

questions.stem: Moses was not allowed to lead the Israelites into Canaan mainly because
options: he broke the tablets of the law
he did not obey God exactly when he struck the rock at Meribah instead of speaking to it
questions.explanation: Numbers 20:7-12 records that Moses and Aaron failed to sanctify God before the people at Meribah.

questions.stem: Joshua succeeded Moses as leader of Israel. He was the son of
questions.explanation: Joshua the son of Nun had been Moses' minister.

questions.stem: The woman of Jericho who hid the two spies sent by Joshua was
questions.explanation: Rahab hid the spies and was spared when Jericho fell (Joshua 2; 6).

questions.stem: During the crossing of the Jordan, the waters stopped flowing when
options: Joshua struck the river with his rod
the people shouted with a great shout
the feet of the priests bearing the ark touched the edge of the river
questions.explanation: Joshua 3:15-16 records that the waters stood still when the priests' feet dipped into the river.

questions.stem: Israel was defeated at Ai because
options: the spies had lied to Joshua
Achan had taken some of the devoted things from Jericho
the priests had refused to carry the ark
the people had worshipped the golden calf
questions.explanation: Achan's secret sin brought defeat on all Israel (Joshua 7).

questions.stem: At Shechem, Joshua challenged the people, 'Choose this day whom you will serve.' This shows that a leader should
options: force people to worship by threats
leave religious matters to the priests only
set a personal example and call people to commitment to God
allow people to serve any god
questions.explanation: Joshua declared, 'As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD' (Joshua 24:15).

questions.stem: Deborah judged Israel while sitting under a palm tree between
questions.explanation: Judges 4:5 places Deborah's palm tree in the hill country of Ephraim between Ramah and Bethel.

questions.stem: Deborah summoned Barak to lead Israel's army against
options: Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army
questions.explanation: Jabin king of Canaan oppressed Israel through his commander Sisera, who had nine hundred chariots of iron (Judges 4).

questions.stem: Barak agreed to go to battle only if Deborah went with him. Deborah then told him that
options: he would become king of Israel
he would die in the battle
the LORD would sell Sisera into the hand of a woman
the battle would last seven years
questions.explanation: Judges 4:9 foretells that the glory would go to a woman; Jael killed Sisera.

questions.stem: Sisera was killed by
options: Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite
questions.explanation: Jael drove a tent peg into Sisera's temple while he slept (Judges 4:21).

questions.stem: Which of the following best shows Deborah's leadership quality?
options: She fought alone without any army
She took the crown from Barak
She relied on chariots of iron for victory
She combined the roles of prophetess, judge and military motivator in obedience to God
questions.explanation: Deborah delivered God's word, settled disputes and inspired Barak and Israel to victory.

questions.stem: The sons of Eli who served as priests at Shiloh were
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:12 calls Hophni and Phinehas worthless men who had no regard for the LORD.

questions.stem: Eli's sons sinned against God by
options: selling the ark to the Philistines
taking the meat of the sacrifice by force before the fat was burnt
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:12-17 says their servant took meat by force, treating the offering with contempt.

questions.stem: When Eli saw Hannah praying silently in the temple at Shiloh, he thought she was
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:13-14: Eli took her for a drunken woman.

questions.stem: Samuel answered the LORD's call by saying,
options: 'Who am I that I should go?'
'Depart from me, for I am a sinful man'
questions.explanation: Following Eli's instruction, Samuel answered, 'Speak, for thy servant hears' (1 Samuel 3:10).

questions.stem: When Eli heard that the ark of God had been captured, he
options: fell backward from his seat, broke his neck and died
tore his clothes and went to war
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 4:18 records Eli's death at ninety-eight years old.

questions.stem: The wife of Phinehas named her newborn son Ichabod, which means
questions.explanation: She named him Ichabod because the ark had been captured and her husband and father-in-law were dead (1 Samuel 4:21).

questions.stem: The elders of Israel asked Samuel for a king partly because
options: Samuel's sons Joel and Abijah took bribes and perverted justice
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 8:1-5: Samuel's sons did not walk in his ways.

questions.stem: The main lesson for parents from the story of Eli is that
options: children should be left to choose their own ways
parents must firmly correct their children, or the whole family may suffer
only the children are punished for their sins
questions.explanation: Eli honoured his sons above God and failed to restrain them, so judgment came upon his house (1 Samuel 3:13).

questions.stem: Saul, the first king of Israel, was the son of
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:1-2 introduces Saul the son of Kish of the tribe of Benjamin.

questions.stem: At Gilgal, Saul disobeyed God when he
options: offered the burnt offering himself instead of waiting for Samuel
spared the king of the Amalekites
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 13:8-14: Saul grew impatient and offered the sacrifice; Samuel said his kingdom would not continue.

questions.stem: God commanded Saul to destroy the Amalekites completely, but Saul
options: spared King Agag and the best of the sheep and oxen
killed all the animals but spared the soldiers
made a treaty with the Amalekites
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:9 records Saul's partial obedience.

questions.stem: When Saul said he had kept the best animals to sacrifice to the LORD, Samuel replied,
options: 'The LORD is pleased with your offering'
'Go in peace; your sin is forgiven'
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:22 teaches that obedience matters more to God than ritual offerings.

questions.stem: After the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, he was troubled by an evil spirit and was soothed when
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 16:23: when David played, Saul was refreshed and the evil spirit departed.

questions.stem: When the LORD did not answer him before his last battle with the Philistines, Saul consulted
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28 records Saul's visit to the medium of Endor, which the law forbade.

questions.stem: Saul died on Mount Gilboa when he
options: was killed in his sleep by David
fell upon his own sword after being badly wounded
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 31:4: rather than be abused by the Philistines, Saul fell on his sword.

questions.stem: Which of the following was a consequence of Saul's disobedience?
options: His son Jonathan became king after him
Samuel anointed him a second time
God rejected him from being king and the kingdom was given to another
questions.explanation: Samuel declared that because Saul rejected the word of the LORD, the LORD had rejected him (1 Samuel 15:23).

questions.topic: David's submission to the will of God
questions.stem: David spared Saul's life in a cave at Engedi, but secretly
options: cut off the skirt of Saul's robe
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 24:4 records that David cut off the skirt of Saul's robe.

questions.topic: David's submission to the will of God
questions.stem: David refused to kill Saul when he had the chance because
questions.explanation: David would not stretch out his hand against the LORD's anointed (1 Samuel 24:6; 26:11).

questions.topic: David's submission to the will of God
questions.stem: In the wilderness of Ziph, David proved to Saul that he had spared his life by taking
options: Saul's spear and jar of water
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 26:12: David took the spear and the jar of water from Saul's head.

questions.stem: The husband of Bathsheba whom David caused to be killed in battle was
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 11 records David's plot against Uriah.

questions.stem: The prophet whom God sent to rebuke David for his sin with Bathsheba was
questions.explanation: Nathan told the parable of the rich man and the poor man's ewe lamb (2 Samuel 12).

questions.stem: In Nathan's parable, the rich man took the poor man's
questions.explanation: The rich man spared his own flocks and took the poor man's single lamb, as David took Uriah's wife.

questions.stem: When Nathan confronted him, David responded by
options: confessing, 'I have sinned against the LORD'
questions.explanation: David's immediate confession (2 Samuel 12:13) is a model of repentance.

questions.stem: Although David was forgiven, which consequence of his sin did Nathan announce?
options: David would be removed from the throne
Israel would be defeated by Syria
The child born to Bathsheba would die
questions.explanation: God forgave David but the child died (2 Samuel 12:14-18), showing that sin has consequences.

questions.stem: When God appeared to Solomon in a dream at Gibeon, Solomon asked for
options: an understanding mind to govern God's people
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:9: Solomon asked for an understanding mind to discern between good and evil.

questions.stem: God was pleased with Solomon's request at Gibeon and also gave him
options: a son who became a prophet
riches and honour which he had not asked for
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:13 promises riches and honour in addition to wisdom.

questions.stem: Solomon discovered the real mother of the living child by
options: ordering the child to be divided into two with a sword
questions.explanation: The true mother's compassion revealed her when she gave up the child to save his life (1 Kings 3:16-28).

questions.topic: The unwise decision of Solomon and Rehoboam
questions.stem: Solomon's heart was turned away from the LORD mainly because
options: his many foreign wives led him to worship their gods
he lost a war against Egypt
he forgot the dream at Gibeon
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:1-8: his foreign wives turned his heart after other gods.

questions.topic: The unwise decision of Solomon and Rehoboam
questions.stem: The prophet who tore his new garment into twelve pieces and gave ten to Jeroboam was
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:29-31 symbolised the division of the kingdom.

questions.topic: The unwise decision of Solomon and Rehoboam
questions.stem: At Shechem, Rehoboam answered the people harshly after he
options: rejected the advice of the old men and followed the young men
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:8-14 shows the danger of ignoring experienced counsel.

questions.topic: The unwise decision of Solomon and Rehoboam
questions.stem: Rehoboam told the people, 'My father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:14 records Rehoboam's harsh reply.

questions.topic: The unwise decision of Solomon and Rehoboam
questions.stem: The immediate result of Rehoboam's unwise decision was that
options: the ten northern tribes rebelled and made Jeroboam their king
all twelve tribes remained united under him
questions.explanation: Israel split into the northern kingdom (Israel) and the southern kingdom (Judah) (1 Kings 12:16-20).

questions.stem: King Ahab married Jezebel, the daughter of
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 16:31 records Ahab's marriage to Jezebel.

questions.stem: Religious tension in Israel during Ahab's reign arose mainly because
options: the temple in Jerusalem was destroyed
Ahab and Jezebel promoted the worship of Baal
the priests refused to offer sacrifices
the prophets of the LORD worshipped idols
questions.explanation: Ahab built an altar for Baal in Samaria and Jezebel killed the prophets of the LORD (1 Kings 16; 18).

questions.stem: Obadiah, the steward of Ahab's household, showed his faith in the LORD by
options: hiding a hundred prophets in caves and feeding them
building an altar on Mount Carmel
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:4 records Obadiah's courage.

questions.stem: During the drought announced by Elijah, he was first fed
options: by ravens at the brook Cherith
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:4-6: ravens brought him bread and meat.

questions.stem: How many prophets of Baal did Elijah face on Mount Carmel?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:22 gives 450 prophets of Baal (with 400 prophets of Asherah mentioned in 18:19).

questions.stem: To make the miracle on Mount Carmel more convincing, Elijah
options: lit the fire with a torch
asked the prophets of Baal to pray for him
offered two bulls instead of one
had water poured on the offering and the wood three times
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:33-35: the trench was filled with water.

questions.stem: After the fire of the LORD fell on Mount Carmel, the people cried,
options: 'The LORD, he is God; the LORD, he is God'
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:39 records the people's confession.

questions.stem: Elijah mocked the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel by suggesting that Baal
options: might be musing, gone aside, on a journey or asleep
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:27 shows the powerlessness of idols.

questions.stem: The vineyard that King Ahab wanted from Naboth was situated
options: in Samaria, beside the temple of Baal
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21:1-2: Ahab wanted it for a vegetable garden because it was near his house; Naboth would not give up his fathers' inheritance.

questions.stem: Jezebel had Naboth killed by
options: arranging false witnesses who accused him of cursing God and the king
sending soldiers to his house at night
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21:8-13: letters in Ahab's name led to Naboth's stoning.

questions.stem: Elijah told Ahab that dogs would lick his blood
options: in the place where dogs licked up the blood of Naboth
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21:19 pronounced judgment on Ahab's greed and injustice.

questions.stem: Why did God delay the disaster pronounced on Ahab's house until the days of his son?
options: Ahab humbled himself, tore his clothes and fasted
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21:27-29: because Ahab humbled himself, the evil was postponed.

questions.stem: Naaman, who was healed of leprosy by Elisha, was the commander of the army of
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:1 describes Naaman as commander of the army of the king of Syria.

questions.stem: Elisha told Naaman to wash in the Jordan
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:10: wash seven times and your flesh shall be restored.

questions.stem: Gehazi lied to Naaman and asked for
options: a talent of silver and two festal garments
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:22 records Gehazi's request; Naaman urged him to take two talents.

questions.stem: The punishment of Gehazi for his greed and lies was that
options: the leprosy of Naaman clung to him and his descendants for ever
he was sold as a slave
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:27 shows the consequence of greed and deceit.

questions.topic: Religious reforms: the reign of King Josiah
questions.stem: Josiah began to reign as king of Judah at the age of
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:1: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign.

questions.topic: Religious reforms: the reign of King Josiah
questions.stem: The book of the law was found in the house of the LORD during Josiah's reign by
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:8: Hilkiah found it and gave it to Shaphan.

questions.topic: Religious reforms: the reign of King Josiah
questions.stem: When the book of the law was read to him, Josiah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:11: Josiah's grief showed his recognition of the nation's sin.

questions.topic: Religious reforms: the reign of King Josiah
questions.stem: Josiah sent his officials to enquire of the LORD through
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:14: they went to Huldah, wife of Shallum.

questions.topic: Religious reforms: the reign of King Josiah
questions.stem: Which of the following was part of Josiah's reforms?
options: Restoring the golden calves at Bethel
Removing the vessels made for Baal and Asherah from the temple and burning them
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 23 lists the cleansing of the temple and the land.

questions.topic: Religious reforms: the reign of King Josiah
questions.stem: After his reforms, Josiah commanded the people to keep
options: the Passover as written in the book of the covenant
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 23:21-23: no such Passover had been kept since the days of the judges.

questions.topic: Religious reforms: the reign of King Josiah
questions.stem: King Josiah died at Megiddo in battle against
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 23:29 records his death.

questions.stem: Nehemiah held the office of
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 1:11 says he was cupbearer to the king.

questions.stem: Nehemiah's brother Hanani reported that the survivors in Judah were in great trouble and
options: the temple had been rebuilt in gold
the people had returned to Egypt
the Persians had made Jerusalem their capital
the wall of Jerusalem was broken down and its gates destroyed by fire
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 1:3 describes the shame of the city.

questions.stem: When Nehemiah heard of the condition of Jerusalem, he first
options: went to Jerusalem immediately without permission
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 1:4 shows prayer as his first response.

questions.topic: Response to the state of the nation
questions.stem: On arrival in Jerusalem, Nehemiah inspected the walls
options: publicly with the governor of the province
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 2:12-15: he told no one what God had put into his heart.

questions.topic: Response to the state of the nation
questions.stem: Which of the following opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding of the wall?
questions.explanation: Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite and Geshem the Arab mocked and threatened the builders.

questions.topic: Response to the state of the nation
questions.stem: Because of threats, each of the builders of the wall
options: worked with one hand and held a weapon in the other
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 4:17 shows vigilance combined with work.

questions.topic: Response to the state of the nation
questions.stem: The wall of Jerusalem under Nehemiah was completed in
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 6:15 records completion in fifty-two days.

questions.topic: Response to the state of the nation
questions.stem: Nehemiah showed concern for the poor by
options: making the nobles stop exacting interest and restore the people's fields
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 5 records his economic reforms; he himself did not take the governor's food allowance.

questions.stem: Daniel and his three friends refused the king's rich food and wine and asked instead for
questions.explanation: Daniel 1:12: they were tested for ten days on vegetables and water.

questions.stem: The Babylonian names given to Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah were
questions.explanation: Daniel 1:7 records the new names; Daniel was called Belteshazzar.

questions.stem: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego were thrown into the burning fiery furnace because they
options: refused to worship the golden image set up by Nebuchadnezzar
questions.explanation: Daniel 3 records their refusal to worship the image.

questions.stem: Their reply, 'But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods', shows that
options: they wanted to bargain with the king
their faith did not depend on whether God delivered them
they were afraid of the furnace
questions.explanation: Daniel 3:18 expresses unconditional faith in God.

questions.stem: When Nebuchadnezzar looked into the furnace he saw
options: four men walking unhurt, the fourth like a son of the gods
an angel quenching the fire with water
questions.explanation: Daniel 3:25 records the king's astonishment.

questions.stem: Daniel was thrown into the den of lions because he
options: refused to eat the king's food
continued to pray to God three times a day against the king's decree
interpreted the writing on the wall
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:10 shows Daniel's faithfulness in prayer.

questions.stem: After Daniel was delivered from the lions, King Darius
options: decreed that people should tremble and fear before the God of Daniel
questions.explanation: Daniel 6:26 shows how faith led to the king's acknowledgment of God.

questions.stem: The main lesson of the stories of Daniel and his friends for Christians today is that
options: it is wrong to serve a foreign government
faithfulness to God should be maintained even at personal risk
God always prevents believers from suffering
questions.explanation: Daniel served the king loyally but obeyed God first, even under threat of death.

questions.topic: True religion and social justice - Amos
questions.stem: Before his call, Amos was
options: a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore trees from Tekoa
questions.explanation: Amos 1:1; 7:14 describe his occupation.

questions.topic: True religion and social justice - Amos
questions.stem: Amos condemned Israel because they
options: sold the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of shoes
questions.explanation: Amos 2:6 attacks corruption and oppression of the poor.

questions.topic: True religion and social justice - Amos
questions.stem: Amos called the wealthy women of Samaria who oppressed the poor
questions.explanation: Amos 4:1 condemns their luxury at the expense of the needy.

questions.topic: True religion and social justice - Amos
questions.stem: 'Let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.' This statement of Amos teaches that
options: true worship must be accompanied by justice
sacrifice is more important than justice
rain is a sign of God's anger
questions.explanation: Amos 5:21-24: God rejects feasts and offerings without justice.

questions.topic: True religion and social justice - Amos
questions.stem: The priest of Bethel who told Amos to flee to Judah and stop prophesying was
questions.explanation: Amos 7:10-13 records Amaziah's opposition.

questions.stem: God commanded the prophet Hosea to marry
questions.explanation: Hosea 1:3 names his wife Gomer.

questions.stem: Hosea's daughter was named Lo-ruhamah, which means
questions.explanation: Hosea 1:6: God would no longer have pity on Israel; Lo-ammi means 'Not my people'.

questions.stem: Hosea's marriage to an unfaithful wife symbolised
options: the exile of Judah to Egypt
Israel's unfaithfulness to God, who still loved her
questions.explanation: Hosea's love for Gomer pictures God's steadfast love for faithless Israel.

questions.stem: According to Hosea 6:6, God desires
questions.explanation: God values loyal love and knowledge of him above ritual.

questions.stem: 'When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.' This passage in Hosea emphasises
options: God's tender, parental love for Israel
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:1 recalls the Exodus as an act of fatherly love.

questions.stem: John the Baptist's food in the wilderness was
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:4 and Mark 1:6 describe his simple diet and clothing of camel's hair.

questions.stem: When Jesus came to be baptised, John at first tried to prevent him, saying,
options: 'I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?'
'Go and show yourself to the priest'
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:14 shows John's humility.

questions.stem: Jesus told John that he should be baptised
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:15: Jesus identified with sinners and obeyed God's plan, though he was sinless.

questions.stem: At the baptism of Jesus, the Spirit of God descended on him
questions.explanation: The Spirit descended like a dove (Matthew 3:16); tongues of fire belong to Pentecost.

questions.stem: The voice from heaven at Jesus' baptism said, 'This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.' Its significance was that
options: God publicly confirmed Jesus' identity and approved his mission
Jesus became God's son only at that moment
John was to become the Messiah
the Pharisees were to baptise Jesus' disciples
questions.explanation: The voice declared Jesus' sonship and God's approval at the start of his ministry.

questions.stem: After his baptism, Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness, where he fasted for
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:2 records the forty-day fast.

questions.stem: When the devil told Jesus to command stones to become bread, Jesus replied,
options: 'You shall not tempt the Lord your God'
'My food is to do the will of him who sent me'
'Man shall not live by bread alone'
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:4 quotes Deuteronomy 8:3.

questions.stem: The devil took Jesus to the pinnacle of the temple and tempted him to
options: worship the devil for the kingdoms of the world
throw himself down so that angels would bear him up
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:5-6: Jesus refused to put God to the test.

questions.stem: In answering all three temptations, Jesus
questions.explanation: Each reply begins 'It is written', quoting Deuteronomy.

questions.stem: The temptation in which the devil offered Jesus all the kingdoms of the world was a test of
options: whether Jesus could read the Scriptures
whether Jesus would gain power by worshipping someone other than God
questions.explanation: Jesus replied, 'You shall worship the Lord your God and him only shall you serve' (Matthew 4:10).

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: When Jesus called Simon and Andrew, they were
options: casting a net into the sea
questions.explanation: Mark 1:16-18: they were fishermen; Jesus said he would make them fishers of men.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: James and John, who left their father in the boat to follow Jesus, were the sons of
questions.explanation: Mark 1:19-20 records their call.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: Levi (Matthew) was sitting at the tax office when Jesus called him. Levi's call shows that
options: Jesus called people regarded as sinners into his service
tax collectors were respected by the Pharisees
questions.explanation: Jesus ate with tax collectors and sinners, saying he came to call sinners.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: According to Jesus, anyone who wants to follow him must
options: deny himself, take up his cross and follow him
questions.explanation: Mark 8:34 states the demand of self-denial.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship

questions.explanation: Luke 9:62 demands undivided commitment.

questions.explanation: Luke 9:57-58 warns of the cost of following Jesus.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: The rich young man went away sorrowful after Jesus told him to sell what he had and give to the poor because

he was afraid of the Pharisees
questions.explanation: Mark 10:22: his wealth hindered him from discipleship.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem: Jesus' parables of a man building a tower and a king going to war (Luke 14) teach that a would-be disciple should
options: count the cost before committing himself
questions.explanation: Luke 14:28-33 urges careful consideration of the demands of discipleship.

questions.explanation: Matthew 18:32-35: God will not forgive those who do not forgive.

questions.explanation: Mark 2:5; the scribes thought this was blasphemy.

five hundred denarii and fifty denarii
thirty and sixty pieces of silver
questions.explanation: Luke 7:41-43: the one forgiven more loves more.

questions.stem: In the Lord's Prayer, Christians ask God to forgive their debts
options: as they also have forgiven their debtors
because they have kept the law
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:12, 14-15 links God's forgiveness to forgiving others.

questions.stem: On the cross, Jesus prayed, 'Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.' This prayer teaches Christians to

questions.stem: The father in the parable of the prodigal son (Luke 15) represents

a strict judge who demands payment

questions.explanation: Mark 14:33 names the inner circle.

questions.stem: In Gethsemane Jesus prayed, 'Remove this cup from me; yet not what I will, but what thou wilt.' This shows
options: his wish to escape to Galilee
his complete submission to the will of the Father
questions.explanation: Mark 14:36 shows Jesus accepting God's will.

questions.stem: Judas identified Jesus to the crowd that came to arrest him by
questions.explanation: Mark 14:44-45: the kiss was the agreed sign.

questions.stem: According to Luke, when one of the disciples cut off the right ear of the high priest's slave, Jesus
options: called down fire on the crowd
touched his ear and healed him
questions.explanation: Luke 22:50-51 shows Jesus' compassion even at his arrest.

questions.stem: How many times did Peter deny Jesus, as Jesus had foretold?
questions.explanation: Jesus foretold that Peter would deny him three times (Mark 14:30).

questions.stem: In the courtyard of the high priest, Peter was first recognised as a follower of Jesus by

questions.explanation: Mark 14:72; Luke adds that the Lord turned and looked at Peter (Luke 22:61).

admitted that he had stolen from the temple
called himself a prophet of Baal
said that they would see the Son of man seated at the right hand of Power
questions.explanation: Mark 14:61-64: Jesus affirmed he was the Christ, the Son of the Blessed.

questions.stem: According to Luke, Pilate sent Jesus to Herod because
options: Jesus was a Galilean and so under Herod's jurisdiction
questions.explanation: Luke 23:6-7 records this move.

questions.stem: Pilate's wife sent a message to him saying,
options: 'Have nothing to do with that righteous man'
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:19: she had suffered much over him in a dream.

he was about to release Jesus
he considered himself innocent of Jesus' blood
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:24; yet he still handed Jesus over to be crucified.

questions.stem: The man of Cyrene who was compelled to carry the cross of Jesus was
questions.explanation: Mark 15:21 names Simon of Cyrene.

questions.explanation: Mark 15:22 translates Golgotha.

'Truly, I say to you, today you will be with me in Paradise'
questions.explanation: Luke 23:43 shows Jesus' mercy to the penitent criminal.

questions.stem: At the death of Jesus, the curtain of the temple
options: was torn in two, from top to bottom
was carried away by the priests
questions.explanation: Mark 15:38 signifies open access to God.

questions.stem: The member of the council who asked Pilate for the body of Jesus and laid it in a tomb was
questions.explanation: Mark 15:43-46; John adds that Nicodemus brought myrrh and aloes.

questions.stem: According to Mark, the women who went to the tomb with spices early on the first day of the week were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and
questions.explanation: Mark 16:1 names the three women.

questions.stem: On the road to Emmaus, the risen Jesus was recognised by the two disciples when he
options: took bread, blessed and broke it
questions.explanation: Luke 24:30-31: their eyes were opened in the breaking of bread.

questions.stem: When Thomas saw the risen Jesus and his wounds, he exclaimed,
questions.explanation: John 20:28 is Thomas' confession of faith.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the main significance of the resurrection of Jesus for Christians?
options: It confirms Jesus' victory over death and gives believers hope of eternal life
It shows that Jesus did not really die
It ended the Roman occupation of Judea
It made the temple sacrifices compulsory
questions.explanation: The resurrection vindicates Jesus and assures believers of new life.

questions.stem: According to Acts 2:42, the early believers devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and
questions.explanation: Acts 2:42 lists four marks of the early church.

questions.stem: The early Christians in Jerusalem showed fellowship by
options: having all things in common and distributing to those in need

questions.stem: Joseph, a Levite of Cyprus, who sold a field and brought the money to the apostles, was surnamed
questions.explanation: Acts 4:36-37: Barnabas means son of encouragement.

questions.stem: Ananias and Sapphira died suddenly because they
options: lied to the Holy Spirit about the price of their land
questions.explanation: Acts 5:1-11: their sin was deceit, not the keeping of part of the money.

questions.stem: Seven men were chosen in Acts 6 because
options: the Hellenist widows were being neglected in the daily distribution
questions.explanation: The Seven took over the serving of tables so the apostles could devote themselves to prayer and the word.

questions.stem: The lesson of the choosing of the Seven (Acts 6) for the church today is that
options: duties should be shared so that every need is met and the ministry of the word continues
only apostles may serve in the church
questions.explanation: Delegation solved a complaint and preserved unity.

questions.stem: On the day of Pentecost, the Holy Spirit came with a sound like
options: the rush of a mighty wind
questions.explanation: Acts 2:2; tongues as of fire also rested on each of them.

questions.stem: Some people mocked the disciples at Pentecost, saying they were
questions.explanation: Acts 2:13; Peter replied it was only the third hour of the day.

questions.stem: In his sermon at Pentecost, Peter explained the event as the fulfilment of the prophecy of
questions.explanation: Acts 2:16-21 quotes Joel 2.

questions.stem: About how many people were added to the church on the day of Pentecost?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:41.

questions.stem: The speaking in other tongues at Pentecost was significant because
options: it ended the use of Hebrew in worship
only the apostles could understand it
people from many nations heard the gospel in their own languages
questions.explanation: Acts 2:6-11 shows the universal scope of the gospel.

questions.stem: Philip explained the Scripture to an Ethiopian eunuch who was a minister of
questions.explanation: Acts 8:27.

questions.stem: The Ethiopian eunuch was reading from the book of
questions.explanation: Acts 8:28-35: the passage about the lamb led to the slaughter.

questions.stem: Cornelius, whose household received the Holy Spirit in Acts 10, was
options: a seller of purple goods at Thyatira
a centurion of the Italian Cohort at Caesarea
questions.explanation: Acts 10:1.

questions.stem: In Peter's vision at Joppa, a voice said, 'What God has cleansed, you must not call common.' The vision taught Peter that
options: the Jewish food laws should become stricter
God shows no partiality and accepts Gentiles too

questions.stem: The Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15) decided that Gentile believers
options: must be circumcised and keep the whole law
need not be circumcised but should abstain from things polluted by idols, unchastity, what is strangled and blood
questions.explanation: James' judgment avoided burdening the Gentiles (Acts 15:19-20).

questions.stem: Peter and John were arrested after they healed a man lame from birth at the temple gate called
When the council ordered the apostles to stop teaching in Jesus' name, Peter and the apostles replied,
options: 'We must obey God rather than men'
questions.explanation: Acts 5:29.

questions.stem: The Pharisee in the council who advised the leaders to leave the apostles alone, saying that if their work was of God it could not be overthrown, was
As he was being stoned, Stephen prayed,
options: 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them'
questions.explanation: Acts 7:60; the young man Saul approved of his death.

questions.stem: King Herod killed with the sword
questions.explanation: Acts 12:2; Herod then arrested Peter, who was freed by an angel.

questions.stem: At Philippi, Paul and Silas were beaten and imprisoned after Paul
options: cast out a spirit of divination from a slave girl
questions.explanation: Acts 16:16-24: her owners lost their gain and stirred up the magistrates.

questions.stem: The riot at Ephesus in Acts 19 was started by Demetrius because
options: Paul had refused to pay rent
the spread of the gospel threatened the silversmiths' trade in shrines of Artemis
the Jews wanted to make Paul king
questions.explanation: Acts 19:24-27: economic interest drove the opposition.

questions.stem: The magician at Paphos who was struck blind for opposing Paul's preaching to the proconsul Sergius Paulus was
According to James, faith by itself, if it has no works, is
questions.explanation: James 2:17.

questions.stem: James uses Abraham as an example of faith shown by works when Abraham
options: offered his son Isaac upon the altar
questions.explanation: James 2:21.

questions.stem: Besides Abraham, James mentions as an example of faith shown by works
questions.explanation: James 2:25: she received the messengers and sent them out another way.

questions.stem: James condemns a congregation that gives a good seat to a man with gold rings and fine clothing but tells a poor man to
options: stand there or sit at their feet
questions.explanation: James 2:2-4: partiality makes them judges with evil thoughts.

questions.stem: James calls the command 'You shall love your neighbour as yourself'
questions.explanation: James 2:8.

questions.stem: According to James, showing partiality is a serious sin because
options: it is only a matter of politeness
whoever fails in one point of the law has become guilty of all of it
questions.explanation: James 2:9-10.

questions.stem: According to James, if anyone among you is sick, he should call for
options: the elders of the church to pray over him, anointing him with oil
questions.explanation: James 5:14.

questions.stem: James says that people ask and do not receive because they
options: ask wrongly, to spend it on their passions
questions.explanation: James 4:3.

questions.stem: James gives Elijah as an example of effective prayer because when he prayed it did not rain for
questions.explanation: James 5:17.

questions.stem: According to 1 Peter, Christians should be subject for the Lord's sake to
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 2:13-14: to the emperor as supreme and to governors.

questions.stem: 'Honour all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the emperor.' These words are found in
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 2:17.

questions.stem: According to 1 Peter, Christians should use their freedom
options: not as a pretext for evil but as servants of God
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 2:16.

questions.stem: Why does 1 Peter want believers to live honourable lives in the midst of unbelievers?
options: So that believers may become rich
So that unbelievers may see their good deeds and glorify God
So that unbelievers may be punished
So that believers may rule over unbelievers
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 2:12.

questions.stem: According to 1 Peter 3:1, Christian wives may win unbelieving husbands
options: without a word, by their behaviour
questions.explanation: Respectful and chaste behaviour can win husbands to the faith.

questions.stem: 1 Peter teaches that if a Christian suffers, he should not suffer as a murderer or thief, but if he suffers as a Christian he should
options: not be ashamed but glorify God

questions.stem: 1 Peter says that love covers
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 4:8.

questions.stem: According to 1 Peter, Christians should practise hospitality
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 4:9.

questions.stem: 1 Peter compares the devil to
options: a roaring lion seeking someone to devour
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 5:8 calls Christians to be sober and watchful.

questions.stem: In 1 Peter 5, what attitude is required of those who shepherd God's people?
options: Service done mainly for a salary
Willingness, without greed for gain and without domineering
Favour shown to their own relatives
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 5:2-3 describes servant leadership.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the creation of man and woman according to Genesis 2. [9 marks]
(b) State three responsibilities God gave to human beings over creation. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The LORD God formed man of dust from the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living being
2 marks: (a) God planted a garden in Eden and put the man there to till it and keep it
2 marks: (a) He commanded the man not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil
1 mark: (a) The man named all the animals but no fit helper was found for him
2 marks: (a) God caused a deep sleep to fall on the man, took one of his ribs and made a woman, whom the man called Woman
2 marks: (b) To care for and keep the environment (till and keep the garden)
2 marks: (b) To have dominion over and wisely use the animals and resources
2 marks: (b) To be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth / obey God's commands
questions.explanation: God formed man from dust, gave him the breath of life, placed him in Eden to till and keep it, forbade the tree of knowledge, and made woman from his rib as a fitting helper. Humans are stewards who must care for creation, use it wisely and obey God.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe how Joseph rose to become a ruler in Egypt. [9 marks]
(b) Identify three leadership qualities shown by Joseph. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Sold by his brothers, Joseph became a slave in the house of Potiphar, who made him overseer of his house
2 marks: (a) Falsely accused by Potiphar's wife, he was put in prison, where he interpreted the dreams of the butler and the baker
2 marks: (a) When Pharaoh dreamt of seven fat and seven lean cows and seven good and seven thin ears, the butler remembered Joseph
2 marks: (a) Joseph interpreted the dreams as seven years of plenty and seven years of famine and advised storing grain
1 mark: (a) Pharaoh set him over all the land of Egypt, gave him his signet ring and a wife
2 marks: (b) Wisdom and foresight in planning for the famine
2 marks: (b) Integrity and self-control (he refused Potiphar's wife)
2 marks: (b) Forgiveness and compassion towards his brothers
questions.explanation: Joseph went from slavery under Potiphar to prison after a false charge, interpreted dreams there, and was summoned to explain Pharaoh's dreams of plenty and famine. His wise plan led Pharaoh to make him ruler over Egypt. He showed foresight, integrity and forgiveness.

questions.stem:
(a) Narrate the experience of Moses at the burning bush in Horeb. [9 marks]
(b) How did God answer three of the objections Moses raised to his task? [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro, his father-in-law, at Horeb, the mountain of God
2 marks: (a) The angel of the LORD appeared in a flame of fire out of a bush that burned but was not consumed
2 marks: (a) God called him and told him to remove his shoes because he stood on holy ground
2 marks: (a) God said he had seen the affliction of his people in Egypt and was sending Moses to Pharaoh to bring them out
1 mark: (a) God revealed his name as I AM WHO I AM
2 marks: (b) 'Who am I?' — God promised, 'I will be with you'
2 marks: (b) 'They will not believe me' — God gave him signs: the rod that became a serpent and the leprous hand
2 marks: (b) 'I am slow of speech' — God appointed Aaron as his spokesman
questions.explanation: At Horeb, while tending Jethro's flock, Moses saw a bush burning without being consumed; God called him, revealed his name and sent him to deliver Israel. To his objections God promised his presence, gave signs, and appointed Aaron to speak.

questions.stem:
(a) Narrate how Deborah delivered Israel from the oppression of Jabin. [10 marks]
(b) What lessons can Christian leaders learn from Deborah? [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Israel did evil and the LORD sold them to Jabin king of Canaan, whose commander Sisera had nine hundred chariots of iron and oppressed Israel for twenty years
2 marks: (a) Deborah, a prophetess who judged Israel under a palm tree, summoned Barak and commanded him in God's name to gather ten thousand men at Mount Tabor
2 marks: (a) Barak would go only if Deborah went with him; she agreed but said the glory would go to a woman
2 marks: (a) The LORD routed Sisera and his army before Barak; Sisera fled on foot
2 marks: (a) Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, killed Sisera with a tent peg; Jabin was subdued
2 marks: (b) Leaders should obey and rely on God's guidance
2 marks: (b) Leaders should encourage and work with others
1 mark: (b) God can use women as well as men to lead
questions.explanation: Under Jabin's oppression, Deborah commanded Barak in God's name to fight at Mount Tabor; she went with him, the LORD routed Sisera, and Jael killed him. Leaders should obey God, encourage others and recognise that God uses both women and men.

questions.stem:
(a) In what ways did Eli fail as a parent? [6 marks]
(b) Describe the consequences of this failure for Eli's family and for Israel. [9 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) He did not restrain his sons Hophni and Phinehas, who treated the offerings of the LORD with contempt
2 marks: (a) He only gave them a mild rebuke when he heard of their immorality with the women serving at the tent of meeting
2 marks: (a) He ignored warnings from a man of God and from Samuel, honouring his sons above God
2 marks: (b) Israel was defeated by the Philistines and the ark of God was captured
2 marks: (b) Hophni and Phinehas were killed in the same day
2 marks: (b) Eli fell from his seat, broke his neck and died on hearing the news
2 marks: (b) Phinehas' wife died in childbirth after naming her son Ichabod
1 mark: (b) The priesthood was taken away from Eli's house
questions.explanation: Eli let his sons abuse the sacrifices and behave immorally, gave only a weak rebuke and ignored God's warnings. Israel lost the battle and the ark, both sons died, Eli died on hearing the news, Ichabod was born, and the priesthood passed from his house.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the two occasions on which Saul disobeyed God's instruction through Samuel. [10 marks]
(b) State the consequences of Saul's disobedience. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) At Gilgal, facing the Philistines and with his men scattering, Saul waited seven days for Samuel
2 marks: (a) When Samuel did not come, Saul offered the burnt offering himself; Samuel rebuked him for acting foolishly
2 marks: (a) God commanded Saul to destroy the Amalekites and all they had
2 marks: (a) Saul spared Agag and the best of the sheep and oxen, claiming they were for sacrifice
2 marks: (a) Samuel told him that to obey is better than sacrifice
3 marks: (b) God rejected Saul as king and gave the kingdom to David, a man after his own heart
2 marks: (b) The Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul and an evil spirit tormented him
questions.explanation: Saul offered the sacrifice at Gilgal without waiting for Samuel and spared Agag and the best animals of the Amalekites. As a result God rejected him as king, chose David, and his Spirit left Saul.

questions.stem:
(a) Narrate the events that led to Nathan's rebuke of David. [8 marks]
(b) How did David show repentance, and what were the results? [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) While his army was at war, David saw Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah the Hittite, bathing and lay with her
2 marks: (a) When she conceived, David recalled Uriah, hoping he would go home to his wife, but Uriah refused
2 marks: (a) David wrote to Joab to set Uriah in the forefront of the hardest fighting, where he was killed
2 marks: (a) David took Bathsheba as his wife, and the thing displeased the LORD, who sent Nathan
2 marks: (b) When Nathan told the parable of the ewe lamb and said 'You are the man', David confessed, 'I have sinned against the LORD'
2 marks: (b) He fasted, prayed and lay on the ground for the sick child
3 marks: (b) The LORD put away his sin so he would not die, but the child died; the sword would not depart from his house; later Solomon was born
questions.explanation: David committed adultery with Bathsheba and arranged Uriah's death. Nathan's parable exposed him; David confessed and fasted. God forgave him, but the child died and trouble followed his house; Solomon was later born.

questions.topic: The unwise decision of Solomon and Rehoboam
questions.stem:
(a) Describe how Rehoboam's decision at Shechem led to the division of the kingdom. [10 marks]
(b) State two lessons that leaders can learn from Rehoboam. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) After Solomon's death, all Israel came to Shechem to make Rehoboam king
2 marks: (a) Led by Jeroboam, they asked him to lighten the heavy yoke Solomon had placed on them
2 marks: (a) The old men advised him to speak good words and serve the people
2 marks: (a) He rejected their advice and followed the young men, answering that he would add to their yoke and chastise them with scorpions
2 marks: (a) The ten northern tribes rebelled, stoned Adoram the taskmaster and made Jeroboam king; only Judah (and Benjamin) remained with Rehoboam
3 marks: (b) Leaders should listen to wise and experienced counsel
2 marks: (b) Leaders should serve their people with humility and not oppress them
questions.explanation: At Shechem the people asked Rehoboam to lighten their burden. He rejected the elders' counsel and followed his young friends, threatening heavier burdens. Ten tribes broke away under Jeroboam. Leaders must heed wise advice and serve with humility.

questions.stem:
(a) Give an account of the contest on Mount Carmel. [10 marks]
(b) What does the contest teach about the supremacy of God? [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Elijah gathered Israel and the 450 prophets of Baal at Mount Carmel and challenged the people to stop limping between two opinions
2 marks: (a) Each side was to prepare a bull on wood without fire; the god who answered by fire was God
2 marks: (a) The prophets of Baal cried from morning to evening and cut themselves, but there was no answer; Elijah mocked them
2 marks: (a) Elijah repaired the altar with twelve stones, poured water on the offering three times and prayed
2 marks: (a) The fire of the LORD consumed the offering, wood, stones and water; the people cried 'The LORD, he is God' and the prophets of Baal were killed at the brook Kishon
3 marks: (b) The LORD alone is the true God who hears and answers prayer; idols are powerless
2 marks: (b) People must make a firm choice to serve God alone
questions.explanation: Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal: the god who answered by fire would be God. Baal was silent despite their cries; Elijah drenched his altar and prayed, fire fell, and the people confessed the LORD. Only God is supreme and deserves undivided loyalty.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe how Ahab came to possess Naboth's vineyard. [9 marks]
(b) What were the consequences of Ahab's greed? [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Ahab asked Naboth the Jezreelite to give or sell him his vineyard beside the palace for a vegetable garden
2 marks: (a) Naboth refused because it was the inheritance of his fathers; Ahab went home sullen and refused to eat
2 marks: (a) Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name to the elders to proclaim a fast and set two base fellows to accuse Naboth of cursing God and the king
2 marks: (a) Naboth was taken out of the city and stoned to death
1 mark: (a) Ahab went down to take possession of the vineyard
2 marks: (b) Elijah pronounced that dogs would lick Ahab's blood where they licked Naboth's
2 marks: (b) Disaster was pronounced on his house, and dogs would eat Jezebel
2 marks: (b) Because Ahab humbled himself, the evil was postponed to his son's days
questions.explanation: Naboth refused to sell his ancestral vineyard; Jezebel arranged false witnesses so he was stoned, and Ahab seized it. Elijah announced doom on Ahab, Jezebel and his house; because Ahab repented, the disaster was delayed to his son's days.

questions.topic: Religious reforms: the reign of King Josiah
questions.stem:
(a) What led to the religious reforms of King Josiah? [6 marks]
(b) Describe four of the reforms he carried out. [8 marks]
(c) State one lesson from Josiah's reign. [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) During the repair of the temple in Josiah's eighteenth year, Hilkiah the high priest found the book of the law
2 marks: (a) Shaphan the secretary read it to the king, who tore his clothes
2 marks: (a) Huldah the prophetess confirmed that disaster would come on Judah but Josiah would be spared because he was penitent
2 marks: (b) He read the book to the people and made a covenant before the LORD
2 marks: (b) He removed and burnt the vessels made for Baal and Asherah and deposed the idolatrous priests
2 marks: (b) He defiled the high places and destroyed the altar at Bethel
2 marks: (b) He kept the Passover as written in the book of the covenant
1 mark: (c) God's word should guide national life, and leaders should act on it promptly
questions.explanation: The finding of the law book during the temple repairs, its reading to Josiah and Huldah's prophecy led to reform. Josiah renewed the covenant, purged Baal and Asherah worship, destroyed the high places and the Bethel altar, and kept the Passover. Leaders should act on God's word.

questions.topic: Response to the state of the nation
questions.stem:
(a) Describe Nehemiah's response to the news of the condition of Jerusalem. [7 marks]
(b) How did Nehemiah overcome opposition to the rebuilding of the wall? [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) He sat down, wept and mourned for days, fasted and prayed to God
2 marks: (a) In his prayer he confessed the sins of Israel and asked for favour before the king
2 marks: (a) He asked King Artaxerxes for permission, letters and timber to rebuild the city
1 mark: (a) He inspected the walls secretly by night and urged the people to rise up and build
2 marks: (b) He prayed to God whenever Sanballat and Tobiah mocked or threatened them
2 marks: (b) He set guards day and night and armed the workers, who worked with one hand and held a weapon with the other
2 marks: (b) He refused invitations to meet his enemies at Ono, knowing they meant harm
2 marks: (b) He rejected false prophecy urging him to hide in the temple, and the wall was finished in fifty-two days
questions.explanation: Nehemiah wept, fasted and prayed, then sought the king's permission and support, and quietly surveyed the walls. Against Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem he prayed, posted guards, armed the builders, refused traps and false prophecy, and completed the wall in fifty-two days.

questions.topic: True religion and social justice - Amos
questions.stem:
(a) What social evils did Amos condemn in Israel? [9 marks]
(b) Explain Amos' teaching on true religion. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Selling the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of shoes
2 marks: (a) Oppression of the poor and trampling on their heads
2 marks: (a) Bribery and perversion of justice in the courts (at the gate)
2 marks: (a) Luxurious living of the rich, e.g. the 'cows of Bashan' who oppressed the poor
1 mark: (a) Dishonest trade with false balances
3 marks: (b) God rejects feasts, offerings and songs when they are not accompanied by justice
3 marks: (b) True religion is to seek the LORD, hate evil, love good and let justice roll down like waters
questions.explanation: Amos attacked the sale of the poor, oppression, bribery in the courts, luxury built on exploitation and dishonest trade. He taught that worship without justice is hateful to God; true religion means seeking God and establishing justice and righteousness.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the temptations of Jesus in the wilderness according to Matthew. [9 marks]
(b) State three lessons Christians can learn from the temptations. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) After fasting forty days and nights, Jesus was tempted to command stones to become bread; he replied, 'Man shall not live by bread alone'
3 marks: (a) On the pinnacle of the temple he was tempted to throw himself down; he replied, 'You shall not tempt the Lord your God'
3 marks: (a) On a very high mountain he was offered all the kingdoms of the world for worship; he replied, 'You shall worship the Lord your God and him only shall you serve', and the devil left him
2 marks: (b) Temptation can be overcome through knowledge of and obedience to the Scriptures
2 marks: (b) Christians should not misuse God's gifts or put God to the test
2 marks: (b) Worship must be given to God alone; power and wealth should not be pursued at the cost of faith
questions.explanation: Jesus resisted turning stones into bread, throwing himself from the temple and worshipping the devil for the kingdoms of the world, answering each from Deuteronomy. Christians resist temptation with Scripture, avoid testing God and worship God alone.

questions.stem:
(a) Narrate the parable of the unforgiving servant. [9 marks]
(b) What does the parable teach about forgiveness? [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Peter asked how often he should forgive; Jesus said seventy times seven
2 marks: (a) A king settling accounts found a servant who owed ten thousand talents and ordered him, his family and possessions to be sold
2 marks: (a) The servant begged for patience and the king, out of pity, forgave the whole debt
2 marks: (a) The servant seized a fellow servant who owed him a hundred denarii and put him in prison
1 mark: (a) The king summoned him, called him wicked and delivered him to the jailers until he paid all
2 marks: (b) Forgiveness should be unlimited
2 marks: (b) Those who have received God's great mercy must forgive others
2 marks: (b) God will not forgive those who refuse to forgive from the heart
questions.explanation: Jesus told of a servant forgiven a huge debt who refused to forgive a small one and was punished. Forgiveness must be limitless and heartfelt, flowing from the mercy God has shown; the unforgiving forfeit God's forgiveness.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the trial of Jesus before Pilate. [10 marks]
(b) Why did Pilate hand Jesus over to be crucified? [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The chief priests delivered Jesus to Pilate, accusing him of perverting the nation, forbidding tribute to Caesar and claiming to be a king
2 marks: (a) Pilate asked, 'Are you the King of the Jews?' and Jesus answered, 'You have said so', making no reply to the other charges
2 marks: (a) Finding no crime, Pilate sent him to Herod, who mocked him and sent him back
2 marks: (a) Pilate offered to release Jesus under the Passover custom, but the crowd asked for Barabbas and shouted 'Crucify him'
2 marks: (a) Pilate's wife warned him; he washed his hands, released Barabbas and had Jesus scourged
3 marks: (b) He feared a riot and wanted to satisfy the crowd
2 marks: (b) He feared losing favour with Caesar, as the leaders said anyone who claimed to be king opposed Caesar
questions.explanation: Accused of sedition and claiming kingship, Jesus was questioned by Pilate, sent to Herod and returned. The crowd chose Barabbas and demanded crucifixion; Pilate washed his hands but yielded, fearing a riot and Caesar's displeasure.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the events on the day of Pentecost. [9 marks]
(b) State three effects of the coming of the Holy Spirit on the disciples. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The disciples were all together in one place when a sound came from heaven like the rush of a mighty wind
2 marks: (a) Tongues as of fire rested on each of them; they were filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke in other tongues
2 marks: (a) Devout Jews from every nation heard them in their own languages; some mocked that they were filled with new wine
2 marks: (a) Peter preached that it was the fulfilment of Joel's prophecy and that God had raised Jesus and made him Lord and Christ
1 mark: (a) About three thousand repented and were baptised
2 marks: (b) They received boldness to preach
2 marks: (b) They were united in fellowship, prayer and sharing
2 marks: (b) They received power to perform signs and wonders
questions.explanation: At Pentecost a sound like wind and tongues of fire came; the disciples spoke in other languages; Peter explained it from Joel and preached Christ, and three thousand were baptised. The Spirit brought boldness, unity and power.

questions.stem:
(a) Give an account of the arrest and death of Stephen. [10 marks]
(b) What lessons can Christians learn from Stephen? [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Stephen, full of grace and power, did great wonders; members of the synagogue of the Freedmen disputed with him but could not withstand his wisdom
2 marks: (a) They secretly instigated men to accuse him of blasphemy against Moses and God, and he was brought before the council
2 marks: (a) False witnesses said he spoke against the temple and the law; his face was like the face of an angel
2 marks: (a) In his speech he reviewed Israel's history and accused them of resisting the Holy Spirit and killing the Righteous One
2 marks: (a) He saw the Son of man standing at God's right hand; they cast him out and stoned him while Saul watched their garments; he prayed, 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them'
3 marks: (b) Christians should be bold and faithful to the truth even to death
2 marks: (b) Christians should forgive and pray for those who persecute them
questions.explanation: Stephen's wisdom angered his opponents, who brought false charges of blasphemy. After a bold speech accusing the council of resisting the Spirit, he saw Jesus in glory, was stoned, and forgave his killers. He models courage and forgiveness.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain James' teaching on the relationship between faith and works. [9 marks]
(b) Show how this teaching can be applied in a Nigerian community today. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead
2 marks: (a) Wishing a hungry or naked brother well without meeting his needs is useless
2 marks: (a) Even the demons believe and shudder; mere belief is not enough
2 marks: (a) Abraham's faith was completed by works when he offered Isaac
1 mark: (a) Rahab was justified by works when she received and sent away the messengers
2 marks: (b) Christians should feed and clothe the poor, e.g. supporting orphanages and the needy in their neighbourhood
2 marks: (b) Christians should show honesty and diligence at work, not merely profess faith
2 marks: (b) Churches should take part in community service such as sanitation, health and education projects
questions.explanation: James teaches that genuine faith shows itself in action; belief alone, like that of demons, is dead, as Abraham and Rahab show. Today it means practical help to the needy, integrity at work and service to the community.

questions.stem:
(a) What does 1 Peter teach about the Christian as a good citizen? [9 marks]
(b) State three ways a Christian in Nigeria can show good citizenship. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Be subject for the Lord's sake to every human institution, to the emperor and to governors
2 marks: (a) Rulers are sent to punish wrongdoers and praise those who do right
2 marks: (a) By doing right, Christians silence the ignorance of foolish men
2 marks: (a) Live as free men, but do not use freedom as a pretext for evil
1 mark: (a) Honour all men, love the brotherhood, fear God, honour the emperor
2 marks: (b) Obeying the laws of the land and paying taxes
2 marks: (b) Voting in elections and taking part peacefully in public life
2 marks: (b) Respecting constituted authority and avoiding corruption and violence
questions.explanation: 1 Peter urges submission to rulers as God's agents, doing good to silence critics, using freedom responsibly and honouring all people and authorities. A Nigerian Christian obeys the law, pays taxes, votes, and shuns corruption and violence.
